items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And Dan Grissom was playing saxophone. We played -- yeah, Dan Grissom was playing saxophone... in this band was Dan Grissom

ctx.x: Yes, right. So any way, I used to do this, and I had mentioned Dan Grissom. But he used to sing like Louis Armstrong, and my mother stopped him from singing like Louis Armstrong, he made him stop -- he had such a beautiful voice. But any way, he was working with us when he went with Lunceford. My mother had a little trio in Chicago, so I -- I keep bringing my mother up, but she was such a tremendous pianist and she was such a hard taskmaster, because if I would play wrong, anything wrong, she might hit me or…

And she also -- while we were in Chicago she also worked for the Oriental Theatre. She used to do like a rehearsal pianist. At this time they wouldn't have a colored pianist in a band or anything, in a white band, but she did all the rehearsal work for the Oriental Theatre and the Chicago Theatre. She was a fine musician.
